report.title: [Setup guided] Unit disappears when entering payload conveyor
report.body:
### Platforms

Windows

### Build

27713

### Issue

Unit disappears when entering payload conveyor

### Steps to reproduce

Using RTS or manually control a unit entering a payload conveyor.

### Mods used

none

### Save file

Any save

### (Crash) logs

_No response_

### REPRO setup assistance (not part of the upstream report)

A prior local attempt did not obtain a ground unit, so the entry transition was never tested. These notes concern setup and controls only; the original reported symptom above is unchanged.

- In this pre-fix source, core/src/mindustry/world/blocks/payloads/PayloadSource.java supports both Block and UnitType configuration. The vanilla sandbox Payload Source can supply a test unit without building a factory supply chain. Verify its actual unit output before trying the reported trigger, and keep the test scene small.
- core/src/mindustry/game/Gamemode.java distinguishes sandbox (infinite resources) from editor (also instant construction). The editor menu's Edit in Game action is implemented by MapEditorDialog.editInGame. This can help create a setup, but record the mode/rules and perform the actual report test in normal play; setup shortcuts must not manufacture the symptom.
- core/src/mindustry/input/Binding.java defines Ctrl for direct unit control, Shift for command mode, and E for pausing/resuming construction. Inspect the source or Controls screen if unsure. A placement outline is not proof that construction completed.
- The updated input worker supports keys on pointer actions (for example Ctrl-click), plus hold_seconds on keypress for sustained movement. seconds alone is a wait after releasing the keys.
- A unit entering a payload can legitimately stop being drawn as a walking unit. Check the connected transport/output and the same unit's continued existence; do not count normal payload transport as disappearance.

summary: Could not test the reported payload-entry behavior. In sandbox, a Payload Conveyor was identified and placed, but a valid ground unit payload and a connected output route were not configured. No unit entering a conveyor, disappearance, destruction, or downstream emergence was observed.

spec.summary: Reported on Windows: a unit reportedly disappears when entering a payload conveyor. The report states this can occur while using RTS controls or direct manual unit control. No independent reproduction or verification is provided.
spec.observed_behavior: The player reports that a unit disappears when it enters a payload conveyor.
known_preconditions: The scenario involves a unit entering a payload conveyor.
The player reports two possible control paths: RTS control or manual/direct unit control.
A prior local setup attempt did not obtain a ground unit, so the payload-entry transition was not tested.
uncertain_conditions: Whether the report reproduces on the specified target commit.
Whether the affected unit is a valid ground unit payload for the conveyor configuration.
Which specific unit type was used.
Which payload conveyor variant, orientation, configuration, and connected output were used.
Whether the unit actually entered the conveyor versus being blocked, destroyed, redirected, or otherwise removed before entry.
Whether apparent disappearance is normal visual removal while the unit is carried as a payload.
Whether the unit continues to exist in the payload transport chain or emerges from a connected output.
Whether RTS control and direct manual control produce the same result.
Whether the issue depends on map, game mode, rules, team, unit AI state, or payload source configuration.
Whether the stated 'Any save' means a new sandbox map, an existing save, or no save-specific dependency.
Whether the issue occurs on Linux; Linux is only listed as planned evaluation, not as a reported affected platform.
No expected behavior was explicitly stated by the reporter.
reproduction_hints: Create a minimal test scene with a payload conveyor and a connected transport/output path.
Use a known ground unit, potentially supplied through a sandbox Payload Source, and verify the source's configured output before testing.
Record the game mode and rules used for setup and for the actual test.
Test the unit's transition into the conveyor, then inspect downstream transport/output and confirm whether the unit persists or exits.
Test RTS-commanded entry and direct-control entry separately.
Do not treat loss of the walking-unit sprite alone as confirmation of a defect, because carried payloads may no longer be rendered as walking units.
If using editor or setup shortcuts, perform the actual observation under normal gameplay conditions and document the distinction.
required_artifacts: Save file or minimal map containing the conveyor layout and unit source.
Exact unit type and team used.
Screenshot or video covering the unit before entry, entry into the conveyor, and all connected outputs/downstream transport.
Conveyor type, orientation, configuration, and complete connected payload-routing layout.
Game mode, map/rules, and whether editor setup or sandbox tools were used.
Input method and exact actions for each reported path: RTS control and direct manual control.
Confirmation of whether the unit can be found downstream, exits an output, is destroyed, or is absent from the map.
Runtime logs and any relevant console output, even though no crash log was supplied.
Build identification sufficient to map reported build 27713 to the evaluated revision, if applicable.

hypotheses.statement: A valid ground unit entering a payload conveyor is only visually absent while carried and should emerge from a connected output.
hypotheses.prediction: In a minimal sandbox layout with a payload source, conveyor, and output, the unit will be visible before loading and reappear at the output rather than being lost.
hypotheses.observation: Sandbox was started and a Payload Conveyor was placed, but a Payload Source plus a valid ground-unit payload/output chain was not configured. Direct movement moved the player's flying unit away from the test area, so no unit-entry transition was observed.
